pending.title: Claim: Division 296 tax applies to super balances over $3 million
pending.description: The $3 million threshold for the Division 296 tax is commonly cited in media coverage. However,ATO indicates thresholds are indexed annually, so the actual threshold for 2026-27 may differ from the commonly cited $3 million figure. Multiple sources (BDO, Heffron) reference indexed thresholds but don't state the exact 2026-27 figure. This could lead to overstatement or understatement of the threshold.
pending.suggestion: Add to fact-checks.json: claim is $3m threshold, verdict is partially_true because thresholds are indexed annually and the 2026-27 threshold may be different. The indexed threshold should be verified against ATO's annual update.

pending.title: Claim: New minimum 30% tax rate on capital gains from July 2027
pending.description: [SOURCE URL MAY NOT CONTAIN CLAIM — verify before publishing] Headlines frequently cite a '30% minimum tax rate on capital gains' without clarifying this applies to real gains (after inflation indexation), not nominal gains. The budget.gov.au specifies 'minimum 30 per cent tax on gains from 1 July 2027' but this represents the floor rate on actual capital gains after accounting for inflation. Someone paying tax on a $100,000 gain might pay 30% on $40,000 (real gain) rather than on $100,000. The headline rate can be misleading.
pending.suggestion: Add to fact-checks.json: claim is 30% minimum CGT rate applies to all gains, verdict is partially_true because the 30% minimum applies to real capital gains (after inflation adjustment), not nominal gains. The effective tax on nominal gains may be significantly lower depending on inflation and holding period.

implemented.title: Is inflation indexation more favourable than 50% discount for long-held assets?
implemented.description: The change from 50% discount to inflation indexation requires verification. For assets held for long periods, indexation may result in a larger taxable gain than the current 50% discount, depending on inflation over the holding period. This contradicts assumptions that indexation is always better.
implemented.suggestion: Add to fact-checks.json: Clarify that inflation indexation does not guarantee a lower CGT outcome than the 50% discount. Provide examples showing when each approach is more favourable based on inflation rates and holding period.
